reasonToGo: Driftholt's crossing ground. The col here is the only one drawn on the island and the saddle beside it is one of two — the other stands on reported ground — so this is the only walked way between one coast and the other. A party comes over it for the grazing on either flank, for what the marsh yields at the edges, and for the cut platform, which is where this ground's stone is prised out.

hazards.name: The notch wind
hazards.description: Everything crossing the island is funnelled through one saddle and comes out of it at a pitch nothing on either coast prepares a party for. A crew caught in the notch with a load goes down and stays down until it drops. The notch is under a kilometre end to end, which is the only reason that is survivable.

hazards.name: The tectonic cave
hazards.description: The cave under the cuesta is a split in the rock and not a cut by water: it has no floor to speak of, it narrows without warning, and it goes further back than the light does. What is known about it is the first hundred paces.

resources.name: Saddle grain
resources.description: Sown on the sheltered flanks either side of the col, where the meadow is deep and the notch wind goes over rather than through. It feeds the crossing rather than any settlement: no village is drawn on this region, and the island's one village is two regions off.

resources.name: Marsh greens
resources.description: Gathered off the marsh strip at the tidal flat and the estuary head, a twentieth of this ground and the only part of it that yields without being sown or grazed. It is taken between tides and eaten the same day; nothing here keeps.

resources.name: Platform flag
resources.description: Levered off the cut platform where the sea has already loosened the bedding, and carried up whole. The island draws no rock, no scree and no karst in any of its eight regions, so every stone worked on Driftholt comes off an old shoreline or a fallen apron — five such exposures across four of its regions, and this platform is one.

landmarks.name: Withyshallow Saddle
landmarks.description: The notch through the ridge, and with the col below it the only crossing between Driftholt's two coasts that anyone has walked. It is bare, it is under a kilometre end to end, and in the wrong weather it is impassable anyway.

landmarks.name: Geo at Merefall
landmarks.description: The cleft at the seaward foot of the crossing, with the arch standing outside it and the drowned valley running in behind. Boats lie in it while a party is over the saddle, because there is nowhere else on this coast to lie.
